precepts.why:
Feign is a verb that means to pretend, to fake, to give a false show of something. It includes pretending an illness: a lot of sisters get Sabbath sick. It includes faking an emotion, or making up an excuse. Remember the brother who used to go around teaching fake it till you make it? Don't raise that man up; he isn't right. To feign means to pretend: you are a fake brother, you are pretending.

Paul sets the opposite: “Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned.” Unfeigned faith: not feigned, not folly.

The whole end of the commandment is charity from a pure heart and a faith that is not pretended. That is the walk Ezra asks God to remember, and the feigned walk is the one he asks God to think not upon.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
Manasseh says the God of the just “hast not appointed repentance to the just.” Paul says the same exact thing: “Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient.” The law is not made for a righteous man, just as repentance is not appointed for the just.

It is made “for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind”, that is homosexuality, “for menstealers”, child traffickers, “for liars, for perjured persons”, liars under oath before the judge, “and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine”, anything not listed.

“According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.” The law is in accordance with the gospel. You cannot have one without the other.

That list is Manasseh. Under the law of Moses he was condemned on all accounts: he killed babies, he was an idolater and a murderer, he shed the blood of children from one end of Jerusalem to the other, and he was steeped in every evil. He was America, but a king; Epstein, but a king; King Diddy Manasseh. There was no animal he could sacrifice. He was a king worthy of death, and his mindset was, I’m the king, I do what I want. The Lord said, you’re the king? Cool, and threw him in prison.

Yet the Lord appointed repentance unto him, and let him live as an example to us in this time. Most kings and celebrities with that status will not repent. When you are rich you become your own god; they literally call them idols. Oprah said on air she does not respect a jealous God. But Manasseh humbled himself, and that is the lesson.

precepts.why:
These are the kind of people we are trying to persuade to change: “Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane.” It is for our people who are lawless.

“For murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers.” If you knew a brother murdered his father or his mother, you would not treat him the same; your instant reaction is, bro, you cold, who does that? “For manslayers”: imagine being cool with a brother and not knowing the whole time he had bodies on him. But there is repentance for those spirits. These are the spirits we are trying to win over and get to submit to the Lord.

“For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind”: women with all kinds of men, men with all kinds of women, and homosexuality. There is repentance for all of these sins. Some of us are struggling with one, two, three, four, five of these. God damn. We have demons on us.

The only way to get it out is to have one counsellor of a thousand and open up. That is the problem: some of you don't want to open up, and by the time we find out what you are struggling with, it's too late to help. It doesn't mean you can't repent, but it is a lot harder because you kept it secret so long, and by the time you tell us you are already having sex and we have to throw you out. Repent, submit yourself to the Lord, and stay close with the pack.

“For menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine.” How many of us lie? We all lie. Why didn't you come to the Sabbath? My back, I was tired: a lie. Why didn't you come to the new moon? I got off work late: a lie, because in your mind you already said, I'll go next time.

Can you persuade a murderer, a lesbian, a homosexual to change their life? Can you turn a liar or a thief into a soldier? You can, and the proof is that you are sitting in the building. Don't say only Deacon Eythan or Black Rhino knows how to talk to people.

precepts.why:
Exodus 21 shows what Israel was doing. Of a maidservant: “to sell her unto a strange nation he shall have no power, seeing he hath dealt deceitfully with her”. Why is that written? Because we would sell our own people off to the heathen for money, being rebellious, evil and stupid. Then verse 16: “And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, or if he be found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death”. We were doing it, and you got death for it.

Paul brings the same law forward: “Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient”, and he lists them: “For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind”, the homosexuals, “for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine”.

Menstealers goes straight back to Exodus 21:16, stealing people for slavery. In Christ, a man who was a trafficker back then could repent. But if you are involved in child trafficking today, get out of that nonsense.

And that is our history. Loango Bay, where the Portuguese traders came, was on the old maps called the Jews' Bay, because the Jews were there. From that West Central African coast, Loango and Angola, nearly half of all the captives in the Atlantic slave trade were shipped to the Americas and the Caribbean. Menstealing is what was done to us, and the law says the man who did it should surely be put to death.
